name: Kodak Professional Tri-X 320 (320TXP)
notes: One datasheet (F-4017) covers Tri-X 400 (400TX) and Tri-X 320 (320TXP, sheet film on 7-mil Estar Thick base); each has its own sheet file.
Characteristic curves: x axis is absolute log exposure in lux-seconds, as printed; the exposure light is not stated on the sheet, 'daylight' is assumed. No Log H Ref is printed.

curves/v is the 320TXP sheet plot with HC-110 (B), large tank, 1 min agitation, 4 minutes: the processing table (page 4, 68 F large tank) gives 4 1/4 min for HC-110 (B) to reach the contrast index of 0.56; 4 min is the nearest plotted time. Other HC-110 (B) times: v-hc110b-6, v-hc110b-9, v-hc110b-14.

Plot 'curves-d76' (a second page, so a second plot): D-76, large tank, 1 min agitation, 6/8/10/12 min as v-d76-6, v-d76-8, v-d76-10, v-d76-12. The recommended D-76 large-tank time (7 1/2 min at 68 F) lies between the 6 and 8 min curves.

Spectral sensitivity: the sheet has a single plot for both Tri-X films (not specific to 320TXP): effective exposure 0.5 s, diffuse visual. sensitivity/v is the solid curve 'D=1.0 > Gross Fog'; v-d03 is the dashed 'D=0.3 > Gross Fog'. Log sensitivity = reciprocal of exposure (erg/cm2) as printed. Doubt: the legend gives the solid, upper curve (log sensitivity about 2.5 to 2.7) as D=1.0 and the dashed, lower one (about 1.2 to 1.6) as D=0.3, the reverse of what physics suggests (a higher density needs more exposure, so lower sensitivity); the assignment follows the legend as printed. The two curves have the same shape.
Grain: diffuse rms granularity 16 (fine), net diffuse density 1.0, 48 micrometre aperture, 12x; measured in KODAK HC-110 Developer (Dilution B), 20 C. Tri-X 400 = 17.

Push: the sheet gives development times for EI 1250 (2-stop push) of Tri-X 320 sheets in XTOL (large tank 10 3/4 min at 68 F, rotary tube 7 1/2 min), and EI 640 in T-MAX RS machine processing (4 to 6 min at 22 C); no curves are plotted for the push EIs.
